text_fidelity_a: Crystal Growing Kit for Kids - DIY Grow Make Your Own Crystal STEAM Experimental Science Kit for Kids Boys and Girls & Adults - 3 Display Crystal Dome Displays - Science Activity for Kids Nah, I would pass on this. Normally, I would say the end result doesn't matter, it's the process and the family time that counts, but even the process was basically nothing. All you do is stir the crystal powder in boiling water until it all melts. That's it, nothing else for the kids to do. Sit back and wait for the underwhelming results. The crystal forms  a square at the base, so you'll need to break it up in order to fit it on the circular display. The black base and clear dome display are cheap thin plastic. The kind of plastic that is used in packaging that you would normally throw away. The crystal cannot stay still on the base because the dome does not clip onto the base tightly. It just covers the base loosely, so if it moves, the crystal inside moves. We threw away the dome lids, and simply flip the base upside down to use as a tray to hold the crystal, and all it's broken crumbs. That's another thing, it's very brittle. The Science is interesting though. I think I'm most annoyed at the display cases actually. The stock photos make it seem like you're getting glass display cases, or at least acrylic, and the black base looks like hard plastic. What you get is the type of thin plastics used as tray liners in packaging, the flimsy stuff you throw away. 2-Star.
text_fidelity_b: Crystal Growing Kit for Kids - DIY Grow Make Your Own Crystal STEAM Experimental Science Kit for Kids Boys and Girls & Adults - 3 Display Crystal Dome Displays - Science Activity for Kids

And since many kids want/need a night light anyway, this craft also serves a practical purpose.

Assembling these night lights doesn’t take too much time. It really depends on the amount of decorating your child intends to do. Once the handiwork is in place, it is just a matter of snapping the AAA batteries into the case, screwing it shut, and displaying the masterpiece. The finished product is cute and some parents might even choose to add one to their own bedroom. Your child will love this, especially knowing that they created something so cool that mom and dad want to put it on display in their bedroom.

text_fidelity_a:
hand2mind Science Kit Music Maker, STEM Activities for Kids Ages 5-7, STEM Toys, Kids Storybook, Pan Flute, Ocean Drum, and Box Guitar, 10 at Home Science Experiments for Kids We are having fun doing the exercises in this hand2mind Science Kit Music Maker, DIY Kits For Kids Ages 5-7. I would say the age range can be up to age 9 actually. Everything you need to make three instruments is in the kit with instructions on how to make 4. The water xylophone doesn't have any materials to make it, so you'll need your own same sized glass jars/cups and food coloring to do that exercise. I wish the explanations were a bit more simplistic for 5-6 years olds. I feel like this is better geared toward older kids 7-9 to understand the science behind sound. My almost 8-year-old kind of got it, but not really.

In the kit, there's a book that has a story. The beginning of the story doesn't really make sense or tie in at all to the ultimate situation at hand. However, the gist eventually becomes a classroom of kids with their music teacher making instruments for a performance. Once he walks you through the 4 different instruments (only three have materials to make an instrument) then you'll start building your instrument and experimenting with them. I feel like the materials are ok sturdy; however, I have instructed my son to not play with them unless we are doing the experiments (until we are finished with all of them). Simply because I do not want them to become damaged before we get to finish. So far we have completed the box guitar, which was easy enough. We did it together with me mainly explaining the instructions and my son completing the tasks. The only thing I had to help with was folding the box. After that, we went through 3 of the 4 experiments. We'll complete the 4th experiment and then move on to the next instrument at a later date. With COVID, it's been nice and important to stretch science kits like this one out over multiple days. I'm glad I saved this for a rainy day because now we've had something nice and fun to do all while responsibly quarantining.
text_fidelity_b: hand2mind Science Kit Music Maker, STEM Activities for Kids Ages 5-7, STEM Toys, Kids Storybook, Pan Flute, Ocean Drum, and Box Guitar, 10 at Home Science Experiments for Kids

The bags for each mini set are unnumbered, you’ll need to open all at the start. All of them except the bags of round 1x1 plates. The studs are meant to simulate dirt, and you don’t attach them to anything, simply pour them in the pots. I didn’t use the studs, the pots are really full and I couldn’t see the bases anyway.

The pieces mostly stay together on the succulents themselves. But some of the pieces are loose, especially the connections between succulent and pot. To build the sets, you assemble the various succulents and then attach them inside the pot. Most of the succulents clip into the base with bar pieces. Imagine a piece that looks like: —C. Sometimes those clips didn’t hold very well, so sticking a second succulent in was enough to dislodge the first.

Getting all the succulents inside each pot takes some finessing and patience. The finished sets are display pieces, not for play -- they are a bit delicate.

The instructions are usually easy to understand, though sometimes I did have to go back or flip forward to understand where a piece went. Some of the colors are off. For example, dark pink in the instructions are really orange pieces. The color differences made some of the sets harder than others, since I couldn’t always tell which piece to use.

I did like that the set include extra stamen options. Getting to choose my own flower colors among the options, or even mix them, was fun.

LEGO Disney Mulan’s Storybook Adventures 43174 Creative Building Kit, New 2020 (124 Pieces) As a child, I loved pop-up books, so of course I love all of the LEGO pop-up book building kits. The first one (see [[ASIN:B07GYB8D34 LEGO Pop-Up Book]] originated as a fan model submitted to the LEGO Ideas fan-voting site (if you want to participate, just google for LEGO Ideas). This DISNEY MULAN’S STORYBOOK ADVENTURES 43174 BUILDING KIT (New 2020 (124 Pieces)) is a smaller, simpler version of the original pop-up book, but it’s still a lot of fun.

The basic pop-up feature is the arched bridge that goes from the center--the book’s stationary spine, where Mulan’s buildings are--to the little “tea service” island in the left half of the book. The bridge goes up and down on a LEGO hinge, and snaps into place when the book is completely open.

There are LEGO studs strategically placed around the open book, so that the three dolls, Mulan’s pony, and Mulan’s cricket cage can all be firmly attached at once. This way, they don’t rattle around loose (or get lost) when the book is closed to be put away. When the book is open for play, the dolls fit on the bridge, under the arches, and can stand anywhere on the book surface.

The assembly instructions are reasonably easy to follow--just look closely at the pictures. I had to take my book covers apart and reassemble them because I got the left (blue water) and right (white land) sides switched, so that the water was on the wrong side when the book was opened.

There are quite a few stickers, but only a few that need to be carefully placed on LEGO elements. The instructions aren’t terribly clear on where to place the stickers that go onto the book’s interior surfaces (e.g., the swimming Koi fish, the lily pads, Mulan’s bed roll, the campfire, the cooking supplies). You can consult the box photos, or even the photos in the online LEGO Shop, if you want extra guidance for these.

One of my favorite features is the two little tassels or bells that swing from Mulan’s temple-like building. I don’t know whether this is an entirely new LEGO element, or whether it has appeared in other sets, but it was new to me. There are enough LEGO pieces in the set to make the book interesting to assemble; and the book is fun to play with after it’s built.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Disney Mulan’s Storybook Adventures 43174 Creative Building Kit, New 2020 (124 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Nanotechnology Science Experiment Kit Do your kids enjoy science? Mine certainly do and they love anything that is interactive and involves more than simply reading a book. This is why they love science kits the way they do and one kit they really enjoy is the Thames and Kosmos Nanotechnology Kit.

I have purchased countless science kits over the years for my youngsters and my kids have played with each, often with varying degrees of interest. The problem with many science kits is that the package doesn’t really contain enough to conduct the experiments- you are required to supply almost all of the materials, measuring devices, etc. yourself. Another problem is that many of science kits contain experiments that are too simple and don’t really challenge any child beyond the age of six. But with Thames and Kosmos Nanotechnology Kit, my children and I quickly discovered that a store purchased science kit can be fun, challenging, and complete. You know the moment you open the box that this science kit is different and the uniqueness only serves to encourage children to open the manual and start conducting experiments. Just looking at the contents reminded me of the science from high school.

The science experiments in this kit revolve around the world of nanotechnology and they serve to educate children on this tiny, micro world. The experiments deliver on their promises and kids really do learn a great deal. Some of the experiments are actually more complex than expected so if your kids are younger, you may need to step in and offer your assistance. I didn’t mind at all, in part because, as I completed the experiments with my kids, I found that I enjoyed the experience just about as much as they did.

Another added touch I like with this kit is the included game board. This is a great idea, because the board helps to further educate children by showing how different experiments relate to each other. Everything is diagrammed and once kids see the visual representation, they will better understand how each experiment works and how things tie together.

Educational toys are great and make for an important diversion from the mindless drabble so common to most forms of child amusement. Thames and Kosmos Nanotechnology is one of the best science kits I have ever encountered and while the price is a little higher than that of other kits, it is certainly money well invested and it will help develop a child’s understanding and interest in science to levels you never would have thought possible.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Nanotechnology Science Experiment Kit

Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud This is a completely different kind of game and the idea of stars and lanterns is abstract. It says it is easy to learn, but to be honest, don't bring your friends together to learn the game. You should set it up, read through the directions and pretend to have two friends with you to understand what is going on. THEN you can explain the game to your friends. The reason is because you can tell this game was not designed in America, there are a few minor English mistakes. The directions have interesting choice of words. So I'm going to try my best by using parentheses to show the words they used in the directions.

The goal of the game is when a word card is revealed, you try to figure out which dixit (picture) cards match that word--by the picture itself, the color(s), inspiration, characters, etc. Then you mark an X (cross) for each dixit card you feel matches that word. At the same time, you want to choose cards you think your friends will choose. If your friends chose that card too, both of you earn stars (sparks) and so on. If they didn't, then you lose (fall) and stop there. If you marked X for too many dixit cards (hoping to get a lot of points), more likely your friends won't have that same card marked and that will make you lose. You have to work like a team, trying to figure out what your friends will choose and win. (This is what they mean by the word, greedy.) This is a good way to teach kids how to perceive the pictures and THINK of others and what they could be thinking, again a "teamwork." This is where it is supposed to be fun. My daughter liked it, but my son didn't like it.

I have one suggestion for you as parents or caregiver of a child age 8 or over. (Ages for the game is for 8+.) I suggest you form the first few turns, you handpick the words you feel your child will be able to "match" then go from there. You handpicking and seeing a few cards in advance honestly does not change the game. The game actually entirely relies on the other players' dixit card choices.

There is one rule that seems pointless. Of course you need to read the directions first to understand what I"m talking about. Here I go anyway--suppose you "fall" then at the end of the game when everyone is ready to score. If you have some sparks and a super-spark from one of your dixit cards that you marked off (crosses), you wipe away one star (but not the super-spark star) then count the remaining stars (sparks). The super-spark star has the same point value as the other sparks so I'm not sure why it makes a difference to wipe off a star or a super-spark star.

This game is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. It's also created in China and I don't know that it's going to be that great, at least for some U.S. audiences.
text_fidelity_b: Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud

Kids First Big & Fun Microscope Science Experiment Kit | Easy-to-Use Kids Microscope | Ages 4-6 | STEM Experiment Guide and Full-Color User Manual | 72 Images | Extra-wide Eyepiec with Light-up Stage I was disappointed in this microscope, BUT it is for preschoolers. Each part was designed with them in mind. It doesn't magnify much, but it's for the benefit of their eyes. It's also designed so that they don't have to shut one eye to see. It's simple! If you're looking for something more advanced, you'll most definitely want to go another route. This one is more of a toy than a microscope.

For now, we have the microscope and the slides within a basket, and that makes it easy to pull it off the shelf.

To use the light part of the microscope, you have to put in 2 AAA batteries, which are not included. Flip the switch and a light will come on. Just place a slide under the lens. I wouldn't recommend this microscope unless you want it as the most basic introduction to very young children(5ish and under). Even then if they've already been introduced to a microscope, they'll probably be disappointed in this one.

SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for $80.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is large enough to make it feel like a nice machine, but small enough, especially when folded, to port around, which is nice because it lends itself to easy travel. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards seemed kind of flimsy, and didn’t stay on well, so I flew without them. The drone handled test crashes well. The propellers held up well, with only some minor scrapes after hitting the ground and nearby trees. The copter simply hit the ground and the arms folded in on impact.

Quiet - The drone has a relatively quiet sound, and isn't too loud. I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. When executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward or backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button at the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Tuning - This was easy to do, and I liked the tactility of the joystick buttons. I found it worked well.

Camera usability- The quality is good, and it is fun to use. However, I’m kind of in the middle on this, which is why the camera is in both the pros and cons. It does provide an accurate view of what the drone sees, and I didn’t have almost any lag. The picture resolution was nice. It’s not super easy to use, but I was able to figure out most of the controls while flying.

Battery: This had a nice battery life, with about 22 minutes of battery life to 1.5 hours charging time. I didn’t stream video, which I would imagine uses a bit more battery, bt for my medium intensity flight, I was very happy with the flight time, especially considering that they give you two batteries, which could give you about 45 minutes of flight time.

Cons:
Unstable/Jerky Camera - Because the camera is hard-mounted to the drone body, the video is very twitchy and jerky as the drone flies around and tilts, particularly when descending. The video became very shaky. I found myself more inclined to use the photo option over the video though, because of how unstable it was. I also found the field of view to be frustratingly narrow, and wanted a more upwards view from the drone.

Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as set up the camera, one of the main selling points with this drone. I’ve found this is a common issue with Syma instructions, and it just makes the products a lot harder to use. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries

LEGO Star Wars Solo: A Star Wars Story Kessel Run Millennium Falcon 75212 Building Kit and Starship Model Set, Popular Building Toy and Gift for Kids (1414 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This LEGO STAR WARS KESSEL RUN MILLENIUM FALCON BUILDING KIT (75212; 1414 pieces) is a great set—definitely one of my all-time favorites. When completed, the kit produces a large, heavy but solid, fun-to-play-with model of the “Kessel Run” Millennium Falcon that’s featured in the new Han Solo movie (“Solo: A Star Wars Story”, released on 5/24/2018). As an adult, I really love this Millennium Falcon, which has a large removable space shuttle in front that accommodates a minifigure, and two powerful, spring-loaded bolt shooters. The bolts always fly 18” or more (you get four bolts). There is also a gunnery pod for minifigures in the center circular area.

The build is fairly demanding, which makes it a lot of fun for experienced builders. The parts you assemble aren’t always symmetrical, and there are a lot of left- and right-handed components, so you have to pay attention to the instructions as you build. There are some “studs not on top” segments, and some components (like the removable transparent nose cone) that are attached “sideways” to vertical studs. There are also a few items (e.g., the lever-action doors at the top front) that attach with Technic parts.

Most of the “triangular” pieces on the top of the model swing up for easy access to the furnished interior. Inside there are chairs that accommodate minifigures, control panels (done with stickers), coffee bars, and engine parts storage boxes. The stickers aren’t excessive, and are easy to position. (I use a thin, flat, metal spudger to pick up and place the stickers accurately.)

The set has several specialized bricks that I haven’t seen before (e.g., the bricks that form a channel for the space shuttle to slide in and out of the front of the model). It also has some unusual building techniques that are used to link together pieces that are installed along a curved line. The model has four sturdy feet, which allow it to stand on a flat surface with space for the underbody gun turret.

The set has only 1414 pieces, but many pieces are very large (e.g., the triangles that open on top). The finished model is a big, substantial toy (the circle is 12” across).
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars Solo: A Star Wars Story Kessel Run Millennium Falcon 75212 Building Kit and Starship Model Set, Popular Building Toy and Gift for Kids (1414 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Digital Coin Bank Savings Jar - Automatic Coin Counter Totals All U.S. Coins Including Dollars and Half Dollars - Original Style, Transparent Pink Jar UPDATE 6-20-2016:

Filltech read my review and reached out to me to make things right. I really appreciated that! They sent a replacement bank free of charge as the one I received was defective and wouldn't count coins right. The replacement is 100% working and is not as hard to insert the coins. It counts them as fast as you can put them in and it gets the pennies and dimes right every time. I recommend this bank and seller because if it's defective, they will make it right!

I had somewhat high hopes for this coin bank, but it's not 100% accurate. It's main problem is distinguishing between dimes and pennies. As far as I can tell it has a lever that is supposed to detect the size of the coin and add that denomination to the total. It doesn't always work. Dimes and pennies get miscounted no matter how slow or fast you put them in. I put in $2 worth pennies and the count was $2.64 because of it counting some of the pennies as dimes. I corrected the count, then added some dimes, which at least four of them were counted as pennies. I think it's overpriced for this reason. If it kept a better count and the jar was glass and came with batteries....then it would be worth $18. As it stands now it's maybe a $5 bank. It might be alright for some people and I like the design and size of it, but probably will pass on buying it again.

text_fidelity_a:
The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up I think I'm just a bit too spoiled by the Pandemic Legacy games, Kings Dilemma, Crusoe Crew, Above and Below, and the like.

The Adventures of Robin Hood is a fine game that is meant to be a legacy-like experience - you play a pretty straightforward move-around-the-board style game, trying to stay inside the shadows printed on the board, until you need to pop out to land on one of a few dozen removable/flippable cardboard cutout pieces that populate the boards. Once you land there to complete objectives, you read a few lines from a book based on the mission at hand, and sometimes you need to perform well at a little combat or make a decision on what to say.

The game is easy to learn and offers a very different gaming experience for those who are unfamiliar with the aforementioned legacy games. Unfortunately, if you've played those, this one is likely just a bit too juvenile. Reading from the book is fun at first, until you find yourself going through the motions and making very similar decisions about completely uninteresting plot points as you progress. Characters largely say the same things, all lead you more or less directly to where you need to go, and when you get there and succeed, you get a "congratulations" rather than a different gaming experience (like in Pandemic), new challenges (like Kings Dilemma) or even a remarkable story experience (like Above and Below). Everything just kind of plays out on it's own.

If you have an impatient bunch, the "pick the next player" from the bag thing could leave people waiting quite a while between turns.

The other thing I don't like is that the rules are a bit interpretive in terms of how movement and the shadows rules affect players. If you want to play this "by the rules" and you have someone who wants to argue over a millimeter, the rules will allow the fudger to make pretty much any interpretation they wish. Most missions are also very much on the easy side.

As this is aimed at a younger audience (I think - the box says 10+ age), some of this is quite forgivable, but for the mature gamer, you have far better options, even if you're enamored with the theme, as I am, or the legacy style game, as my family is. The little one was bored by the long missions, Mom and Dad were thinking there should just be a little more punch to the story. We found this to be a 2/5 experience, but I think most would find it to be a 3/5 or so.
text_fidelity_b: The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up

text_fidelity_a:
SUPER MARIO Boo's Mansion Kids Halloween Hide-and-Seek Game with 10 Figurines and Accessories We had so much fun with this. While we did not do the whole party element with people watching us unbox, we had a great time just on a normal day when the kids had done a great job, having a special treat of opening up each of the flaps to see what was inside.

A glow-in-the-dark boo, another boo, both with movable arms, a skeleton for around the plant and a dry bones were the highlights for us in this set. The Princess peach, also was detailed to an extent I have never seen on any of our other Princess peach figures. Usually they just fill in and under her skirt with solid plastic, and this one they gave her legs, undershorts, and high-heeled shoes underneath her dress so it is much more of a realistic figure than usual. I think either Mario or Luigi, needed a little plastic stand to be able to stand up and not just topple over. I would've appreciated a little more design on those guys so that they could be played with without an additional little clear plastic stand.

The flap opening and unveiling of the characters was a lot of fun. The characters were almost impossible in some cases to get out of the container without completely destroying the entire packaging, so my kids had to be flexible to wait until we were done opening all the flaps, then tear open the packaging to be able to push from the back and get some of those characters out. However, they were definitely firmly and securely packaged in there and were not going anywhere or getting damaged with those vacuum formed spots to sit.

Overall this was a lot of fun, and with the excellent quality of the figures, made for a very special and memorable gifting event to the kids.
text_fidelity_b: SUPER MARIO Boo's Mansion Kids Halloween Hide-and-Seek Game with 10 Figurines and Accessories

LeapFrog On-The-Go Story Pal Green This reader is pretty neat.
It has a lot of functionality built into it.
It’s also pretty small.
It’s like a portable toddler story/radio!
There are multiple settings
Stories (37), Music/Poems (25), Bedtime (10), Create your own Playlist (allows for 10 minute recordings!).

I think the create your own playlist setting would be awesome for any parent that has to travel a lot or for a service member that is deployed.
The stories are easy to understand and they use voice changes for different characters.
The volume control is nice - I like that it shows the volume number in case the kid is using headphones - you can check the volume without much effort.

If I could change anything about this it would be that it used a USB type cable to charge it. It has a port for downloading additional content from online - but not for charging. It uses 3 AA batteries.
I also wish that during the bedtime setting it would not use the lights on the front screen - the lights are great during day use but not when trying to get the kids to sleep.
It is nice to have the timer setting for bedtime.

text_fidelity_a: CGE Czech Games Edition Codenames Boardgame This game is best played with 4 people (two teams of two).  Your partner tries to prompt you to pick the correct cards on the table between you by giving you a single word clue and telling you how many cards on the table it relates to.  You need to decipher the hint by figuring out which of the cards they means, but don't pick the wrong one!  It could end up giving a point to the other team or if you pick the one "black card" on the table it ends the game and you instantly lose.  This game is endlessly creative and challenging as the word cards on the table and which cards correspond to your team will always be different each game.  The creative part is figuring out new ways to bundle the most cards together with a single word so you can find all your teams cards before the other team finds theirs.  It's a race to figure out the code!

text_fidelity_a:
GiiKER Electronic Bluetooth Speed Cube i3s, Real-time Connected STEM Smart Cube 3x3 for All Ages, Companion App Support Online Battle with Cubers Across The Globe, with Exclusive Charger [[VIDEOID:df61075bc0172b4d34aec64cd5ddd45b]] The concept of smart cubes are really cool: They connect over Bluetooth low power protocol to an app so that your movements are digitized. This opens up possibilities like training exercises and real-time online competitions. The app is actually pretty excellent here, unlike another cube we tried, this one actually has competitors and it seems to work (however my son is suspicious that they might not be real players. They could be AI, because how many people could there really be using this app at the same time he is?).
However, the hardware seems buggy on this. Sometimes the cube will move and the app won't register that movement. Try it again later with the same move, and it does. In the video here, my son demonstrates that it completely loses calibration as he solves the cube. We tried the app on a few different devices in our home, with processors from Qualcomm Snapdragon and other's with Samsung's Exynos (flagship Galaxy S level hardware). It doesn't seem to be the phone/tablet that is the problem, but rather that the cube isn't always registering the movement to send to the app. This causes things to get out of alignment relatively quickly, especially when speed solving, and renders the entire experience frustrating.
This had so much potential, we're really disappointed.

text_fidelity_a:
4M Tin Can Edge Detector Robot - DIY Science Construction Stem Toy For Kids & Teens My kids like their science, particularly my youngest who envisions, among other things, working for the government and taking part in the first mission to Mars. So, given my kids interest in all things scientific, the Tin Can Edge Detector looked like something they would enjoy building and examining from a scientific point of view.

Putting this little machine together takes some effort and one reason it takes more work than it should is the instructions. They are not written as clearly as they should be. It would not have been that difficult for the manufacturer to get this right, but it seems they put little effort into it. You have to supply your own battery and a can, but most importantly, you have to be patient and give it time. It’s also best to have an adult take charge, as young children will grow frustrated if they attempt this on their own.

Once assembled, you just place the robot on a table and let it do its thing. As expected, it moves across the surface until it detects an edge, then it reverses itself. It seemed to have no trouble doing what it claimed, and that is detecting when it reached the table’s edge and not falling off. In that respect, the robot functions as it should.

Now, what about the science? Well, It can teach a little bit about robotics, but that is about the extent of the educational value. There isn’t much else to it. Oh, and green advocates will like that it requires you to provide your own soda can because it encourages recycling

Science is a popular subject with my kids but they had a difficult time getting fired up over the Tin Can Edge Detector. The problem, from a kid’s perspective, is that it doesn’t really do enough to make it interesting. Simply crawling around on a table and not falling off just didn’t cut it for my kids. Adults will dislike the assembly more than anything and the limited educational value is also a drawback. Still, it does offer kids and parents an excuse to spend a little time together and it does what the manufacturer claims, so I’m going to give it a middle rating and a passing grade. There are better educational toys, but there is enough here to keep kids semi- interested for a low price.
